details.question: PostgreSQL 官方文档中，`synchronous_commit=remote_apply` 会让 COMMIT 等待到什么状态？这对只读查询的可见性意味着什么？
details.reference_answer: `remote_apply` 会让每次提交等待当前同步备库确认已经重放该事务；因此事务随后对备库上的用户查询可见。
details.model_answer:
`synchronous_commit=remote_apply` causes `COMMIT` to wait for the synchronous standby to acknowledge that the transaction has been applied (i.e., the data is visible to queries on the standby and written to durable storage). If the primary receives a cancellation signal (e.g., `CTRL+C`) before the standby acknowledges, PostgreSQL reports a warning: [S2](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/84cc0332fadf4f4bb1fff7a169db8ecd58f7911c.camel%40cybertec.at)
> "The transaction has already committed locally, but might not have been replicated to the standby." [S1](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/cac4b9df-92c6-77aa-687b-18b86cb13728@stratox.cz)
The transaction is still considered committed locally, but it is **not** guaranteed to be visible on the standby. [S2](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/84cc0332fadf4f4bb1fff7a169db8ecd58f7911c.camel%40cybertec.at)
**Implications for read-only queries:** [S2](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/84cc0332fadf4f4bb1fff7a169db8ecd58f7911c.camel%40cybertec.at)
- On the primary, the transaction is visible immediately after the local commit (because `synchronous_commit=remote_apply` does not delay local visibility). [S1](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/cac4b9df-92c6-77aa-687b-18b86cb13728@stratox.cz)
- On the standby, the transaction is **not** visible until the standby applies the commit record. Therefore, a read-only query on the standby may see stale data or fail if it depends on the uncommitted data. [S2](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/84cc0332fadf4f4bb1fff7a169db8ecd58f7911c.camel%40cybertec.at)
- If the primary fails before the standby acknowledges, the standby may not have the committed data, leading to data loss or inconsistency. [S2](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/84cc0332fadf4f4bb1fff7a169db8ecd58f7911c.camel%40cybertec.at)

If the primary receives a cancellation signal (e.g., `CTRL+C` or a client abort), PostgreSQL will still report success locally but will issue a warning: [S2](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/cac4b9df-92c6-77aa-687b-18b86cb13728@stratox.cz)
> "WARNING: canceling wait for synchronous replication due to user request [S2](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/cac4b9df-92c6-77aa-687b-18b86cb13728@stratox.cz)
> DETAIL: The transaction has already committed locally, but might not have been replicated to the standby." [S2](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/cac4b9df-92c6-77aa-687b-18b86cb13728@stratox.cz)
This means the transaction is committed on the primary, but the standby may not yet have received or applied it. [S1](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/84cc0332fadf4f4bb1fff7a169db8ecd58f7911c.camel%40cybertec.at)
**Implications for read-only queries:** [S1](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/84cc0332fadf4f4bb1fff7a169db8ecd58f7911c.camel%40cybertec.at)
Because the transaction is considered committed on the primary, read-only queries on the primary will see the new data. However, if the primary fails and a standby is promoted, the standby may not have received the transaction (if the cancellation occurred before the standby acknowledged it). In that case, the promoted standby will not contain the transaction, and read-only queries on the new primary will not see the data. Thus, the transaction is not guaranteed to be visible to all readers in a failover scenario. [S1](https://www.postgresql.org/message-id/84cc0332fadf4f4bb1fff7a169db8ecd58f7911c.camel%40cybertec.at)
